verdict.rationale: ReadMe documents bi-directional sync with GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repositories. It also documents a workflow that runs docs entirely through Git, with Markdown and OpenAPI in the repo and pull requests as the review step. The evidence does not explicitly show that git branches map to ReadMe branches or versions, or that a merge triggers publishing; the documented branches are ReadMe's own in-app branches. missing for 10: explicit documentation that merges to a target branch publish the hub, a git-branch-to-version/branch mapping, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the Git-driven workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, my docs live in my own git repository — branches, pull requests, and merges drive what gets published

citations.quote: Bi-directional sync creates a two-way connection between your ReadMe project and a GitHub or GitLab repository.
Connect your project to a GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repos
Run documentation entirely through Git, with Markdown and OpenAPI in your repository and pull requests as the review step.
Write in your preferred environment whether that's ReadMe or your local development setup.
